newsitem.title: FINLAND: M-Serla, UPM asset swap seen.
newsitem.headline: M-Serla, UPM asset swap seen.

text.p: Finnish forestry groups UPM-Kymmene Oy and Metsa-Serla Oy are highly unlikely to announce a merger later on Tuesday but may signal some kind of asset swap between the companies, analysts said.

The two companies announced they would hold a joint press conference at 1200/1000 GMT in Helsinki after requesting a share suspension on the Helsinki bourse pending news of a "significant corporate arrangement".
"A merger would be highly unlikely, 'significant corporate arrangement' signals some swaps in units or factories," said one, requesting anonymity amid speculation.
"I know Metsa-Serla would be interested in UPM's magazine paper unit, but I have no idea what would be the corresponding unit for UPM," the analyst said.
"My rough guess would be an elimination of cross-ownership in (pulp mills) Metsa-Rauma and Metsa-Botnia -- this is shooting from the hip," said Lars Kjellberg at Enskilda Bank in Stockholm.
Both have holdings in the pulp mills.
"Structurally, this would be a good move for both companies (but) it would not have any significant impact on short-term earnings," he said.
Metsa-Serla said on October 17 that it would focus on packaging and printing and on competitive pulp and on November 6, it announced the sale of its chemicals plants.

After that sale, Metsa-Serla CEO Jorma Vaajoki said it had no plans to sell its tissue unit which has net sales of about 700 million markka, about 15 percent of Metsa's 13.1 billion markka net sales in 1995.
Metsa-Serla produces magazine paper, fine papers, boards and has sawmilling operations.
The biggest constituent of its 9.5 billion markka January-August net sales was printing papers with a 3.5 billion markka turnover, and pulp was second largest at 2.2 billion.
In January-August, its paperboard net sales were 1.5 billion markka, tissue net sales 1.2 billion and packaging 0.8 billion markka.

UPM-Kymmene's largest division is magazine papers -- January-August net sales at 7.1 billion markka of total 33.8 billion turnover -- and it has large operations in newsprint, fine papers, packaging and chemical pulp.
UPM says it uses most of its pulp internally.
This year, all UPM's major units have made operating profits, except the chemical pulp unit which fell into a 285 million markka loss in the second quarter from a 213 million profit in the first.
